title: Microsoft Dataverse: bulk delete gains run details and solution-aware jobs
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, immediate execution of imported jobs, permissions and documented operations are supported. The comparison calling bulk delete one of the few tools for deleting records at scale is unsubstantiated; the control paths and API presentation also need small clarifications.

claims.claim: A bulk delete job that fails or ends prematurely does not roll back records already deleted.
claims.quote: If a bulk delete job fails or ends prematurely, the operation doesn't roll back any deleted records. The record data remains deleted.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Selecting the Bulk Deletion Wizard's Permanent deletion checkbox permanently removes records so they cannot be recovered.
claims.quote: The Bulk Deletion Wizard includes a Permanent deletion checkbox. When selected, records deleted by the bulk delete job are permanently removed and can't be recovered.

claims.claim: For a job using Permanent deletion, enabled deleted record keeping is bypassed rather than moving its deleted records to deleted records tables.
claims.quote: If deleted record keeping is turned on for your environment, this option skips the step of moving data to deleted records tables, which results in faster job execution.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: "bulk deletion" "solution" "role" "admins"; "bulk deletion" "import" "System Administrator". Opened learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/delete-bulk-records; its solution note names only 'admins', not a specific role or privilege.

claims.claim: Running a bulk delete job through the API requires BulkDelete privileges on the table types being deleted.
claims.quote: To run a bulk delete job, you must have BulkDelete and Delete privileges on the table types you're deleting.

claims.claim: Running a bulk delete job through the API requires Delete privileges on the table types being deleted.
claims.quote: To run a bulk delete job, you must have BulkDelete and Delete privileges on the table types you're deleting.

claims.claim: The API caller also needs read permission on the records specified in QuerySet.
claims.quote: You must also have read permissions on the table records that you specify in the QuerySet property.

claims.claim: A system administrator has the necessary bulk delete API permissions by default.
claims.quote: A system administrator has the necessary permissions by default. Grant them to other users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Bulk deletion supports periodic and recurring jobs.
claims.quote:
- Delete data periodically.

claims.claim: Bulk deletions can trigger plug-ins or workflows registered for the affected table's delete action.
claims.quote: If the delete action on a specific table type triggers a plug-in or a workflow (process), the bulk delete job triggers the plug-in or workflow every time it deletes a table record of that type.

claims.claim: The sources describe no agent or AI action for these improvements.
claims.quote: Searched: "bulk delete" "Run details" "Copilot". Read roadmap record and learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/delete-bulk-records; they describe error handling and solution-aware jobs, not an AI or agent action.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rendered controls table
claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center route is Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Data management > Bulk deletion.
claims.quote:
In the command bar, select Settings.
Expand Data management, then select Bulk deletion.
Select New to run the Bulk Deletion Wizard to create a bulk deletion job with the records you want to delete.
claims.fix: For creating a job, extend controls[0].ui.path to 'Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Data management > Bulk deletion > New'. Keep the existing shorter route in the checklist for listing jobs. The cited page documents both.

claims.claim: POST [Organization Uri]/api/data/v9.2/BulkDelete with the printed QuerySet, JobName, SendEmailNotification, ToRecipients, CCRecipients, RecurrencePattern and StartDateTime properties submits a bulk delete job.
claims.quote:
POST [Organization Uri]/api/data/v9.2/BulkDelete HTTP/1.1

Specify the query expressions that describe the records to delete in the QuerySet property of your request.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api.call to 'POST [Organization Uri]/api/data/v9.2/BulkDelete', removing the inline request body. Add to its note: 'The request body sets QuerySet to identify the records to delete.' The tutorial's example and the cited BulkDelete Action reference confirm all seven printed property names.

claims.claim: The route to errors is Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Data management > Bulk deletion > job > Run details.
claims.quote: If a job failed to run, open the latest completed job, and select the Run details tab to view all the errors that were encountered during the job.

claims.claim: pac solution import --path Solution.zip --environment <environment ID or URL> imports a solution into the target Dataverse environment and is a general solution import command.
claims.quote:
pac solution import
Import the solution into Dataverse.
--environment: Specifies the target Dataverse. The value may be a Guid or absolute https URL.
--path: Path to solution zip file.

claims.claim: The roadmap contrasts the new error details with generic failures that administrators previously had to diagnose.
claims.quote: Instead of generic failures, admins can quickly understand what went wrong and why, enabling faster troubleshooting, fewer reruns, and more efficient resolution of large-scale deletion jobs.
